facts.statement: Stenonychosaurus is a disputed genus of troodontid dinosaur with the meaning "narrow claw lizard".
facts.quote: Stenonychosaurus (meaning "narrow claw lizard") is a disputed genus of troodontid dinosaur

facts.statement: The only known species, S. inequalis, was named by Charles Mortram Sternberg in 1932.
facts.quote: The type and only species, S. inequalis, was named by Charles Mortram Sternberg in 1932

facts.statement: The species was originally described based on a foot, hand fragments, and tail vertebrae from the Late Cretaceous of Alberta.
facts.quote: based on a foot, fragments of a hand, and some caudal vertebrae from the Late Cretaceous of Alberta

facts.statement: Fossils are found in the Late Cretaceous Dinosaur Park Formation of Alberta, Canada, and possibly the Two Medicine Formation.
facts.quote: from the Late Cretaceous Dinosaur Park Formation of Alberta, Canada, as well as possibly the Two Medicine Formation

facts.statement: The holotype possesses an enlarged claw on the second toe, a feature characteristic of early paravian dinosaurs.
facts.quote: A remarkable feature of these remains was the enlarged claw on the second toe, which is now recognized as characteristic of early paravians

facts.statement: A more complete skeleton was described by Dale Russell in 1969, forming the basis for a famous life-sized sculpture.
facts.quote: A more complete skeleton of Stenonychosaurus was described by Dale Russell in 1969

facts.statement: Historically, Stenonychosaurus was grouped with Saurornithoides in the family Saurornithoididae.
facts.quote: Along with Saurornithoides, it formed the family Saurornithoididae

facts.statement: In 2017, Van der Reest and Currie validated Stenonychosaurus but reassigned much of the material to the new genus Latenivenatrix.
facts.quote: Later in 2017, Van der Reest and Currie found Stenonychosaurus to be a valid genus, but reassigned much of the known material to the new genus Latenivenatrix

facts.statement: Paleontologist Dale Russell hypothesized that if Stenonychosaurus had evolved further, its brain case could have reached 1100 cm³, comparable to a human.
facts.quote: Russell suggested that if the trend in Stenonychosaurus evolution had continued to the present, its brain case could by now measure 1100 cm3, comparable to that of a human

facts.statement: Stenonychosaurus possessed semi-manipulative fingers capable of grasping objects and binocular vision.
facts.quote: Troodontids had semi-manipulative fingers, able to grasp and hold objects to a certain degree, and binocular vision

facts.statement: It is debated whether the evolutionary trajectory of Stenonychosaurus would have led to human-like intelligence, with critics arguing such a scenario is overly anthropomorphic.
facts.quote: However, Russell's thought experiment has been met with criticism from other paleontologists since the 1980s, many of whom point out that his Dinosauroid is overly anthropomorphic

facts.statement: Stenonychosaurus was a small dinosaur reaching up to 2.5 meters in length and 35 kilograms in body mass.
facts.quote: Stenonychosaurus was a small dinosaur, up to 2.5 m in length and 35 kg in body mass.

facts.statement: Stenonychosaurus possessed very long, slender hind limbs that suggest it was capable of running quickly.
facts.quote: They had very long, slender hind limbs, suggesting that these animals were able to run quickly.

facts.statement: The dinosaur had large, retractable, sickle-shaped claws on its second toes that were raised off the ground while running.
facts.quote: They had large, retractable, sickle-shaped claws on the second toes, which were raised off the ground when running.

facts.statement: Stenonychosaurus had very large, slightly forward-facing eyes that provided depth perception and may have suggested a partially nocturnal lifestyle.
facts.quote: Their eyes were very large (perhaps suggesting a partially nocturnal lifestyle), and slightly forward facing, giving Stenonychosaurus some degree of depth perception.

facts.statement: Stenonychosaurus possessed one of the largest known brains relative to body mass among dinosaurs, comparable to modern birds.
facts.quote: Stenonychosaurus had one of the largest known brains of any dinosaur, relative to its body mass (comparable to modern birds).

facts.statement: The dinosaur had bony cristae supporting its tympanic membranes, which were ossified in at least the top and bottom regions.
facts.quote: Additionally, it had bony cristae supporting their tympanic membranes, that were ossified at least in their top and bottom regions.

facts.statement: The jaws of Stenonychosaurus met in a broad, U-shaped symphysis similar to that of an iguana adapted to a plant-eating lifestyle.
facts.quote: The jaws met in a broad, U-shaped symphysis similar to that of an iguana, a lizard species adapted to a plant-eating lifestyle.

facts.statement: Growth ring counts suggest that Stenonychosaurus reached its adult size in approximately 3 to 5 years.
facts.quote: Age determination studies performed on the Two Medicine troodont using growth ring counts suggest that this dinosaur reached its adult size probably in 3–5 years.

facts.statement: Dinosaur eggs and nests were discovered by John R. Horner in 1983 in the Two Medicine Formation of Montana.
facts.quote: Dinosaur eggs and nests were discovered by John R. Horner in 1983 in the Two Medicine Formation of Montana.

facts.statement: A later analysis found that the type of parental care in troodonts cannot be determined using the conventional allometric methods used by Varricchio et al.
facts.quote: However, a later analysis of avian clutch mass found that the type of parental care cannot be determined using conventional allometric methods such as the one used by Varricchio et al.

facts.statement: The genus Stenonychosaurus was named by C.M. Sternberg in 1932.
facts.quote: genus_authority: C.M. Sternberg, 1932

facts.statement: Stenonychosaurus lived during the late Upper Cretaceous, approximately 76 million years ago in the Campanian stage, in what is now North America.
facts.quote: que vivió a finales del período Cretácico superior, hace aproximadamente entre 76 millones de años, en el Campaniaense, en lo que hoy es Norteamérica.

facts.statement: Stenonychosaurus inequalis was discovered in the Dinosaur Park Formation of Alberta, Canada, and named by Charles Sternberg in 1932 based on foot fossils, hand fragments, and some tail vertebrae.
facts.quote: Descubierto en la Formación Dinosaur Park de Alberta, Canadá, S. inequalis, fue nombrado por Charles Sternberg en 1932, basado en fósiles del pié, fragmentos de una mano y algunas vértebras caudales.

facts.statement: Stenonychosaurus inequalis was reassigned as a synonym of the genus Troodon in 1987 by Philip J. Currie, a decision later reversed by Evans et al. and Van der Reest and Currie in the same year.
facts.quote: S. inequalis fue reasignado como un género sinónimo en 1987 por Philip J. Currie al género Troodon, hecho que fue revertido por el reconocimiento de Stenonychosaurus como un género separado del dudoso Troodon por Evans et al. y también más tarde en el mismo año por Van der Reest y Currie.

facts.statement: Stenonychosaurus was a small dinosaur standing 0.9 meters tall and measuring between 2.4 and 3.5 meters in length.
facts.quote: Stenonychosaurus era un dinosaurio pequeño, medía 0,9m de altura, entre 2,4 a 3,5 de longitud, y pesaba desde 35 a 50kg.

facts.statement: Its very long and thin hind legs suggest that the animal could run very fast.
facts.quote: Tenían patas traseras muy largas y delgadas, sugiriendo que estos animales podían correr muy rápido.

facts.statement: It possessed large sickle-shaped retractable claws on the second toe that lifted while running.
facts.quote: Tenían grandes garras retraíbles en forma de hoz en el segundo dedo del pie, las cuales se levantaban mientras corrían.

facts.statement: Its very large eyes, which pointed slightly forward to provide depth perception, possibly suggest a nocturnal or crepuscular lifestyle.
facts.quote: Sus ojos eran muy grandes, posiblemente sugiriendo un estilo de vida nocturno o crepuscular, y apuntaban ligeramente al frente, dándole a Stenonychosaurus cierta Percepción de profundidad.

facts.statement: It had one of the largest known brains of any dinosaur relative to its body mass, comparable to modern birds.
facts.quote: Stenonychosaurus tenía uno de los cerebros más grandes conocidos de cualquier dinosaurio en relación con su masa corporal, siendo comparable a las aves modernas.

facts.statement: It possessed bony crests that supported its tympanic membranes, which were ossified in at least their upper and lower regions.
facts.quote: Además, tenía crestas óseas que sostenían sus membranas timpánicas que estaban osificadas al menos en sus regiones superior e inferior.

facts.statement: It was first described by Sternberg in 1932 based on a foot, hand fragments, and some tail vertebrae.
facts.quote: El primero en ser descrito fue nombrado Stenonychosaurus inequalis por Sternberg en 1932, basado en un pie, fragmentos de una mano y algunas vértebras de la cola.

facts.statement: The first non-tooth specimens assigned to Troodon were found by Sternberg in 1928 in the Dinosaur Park Formation of Alberta.
facts.quote: Los primeros especímenes que fueran asignados a Troodon que no eran dientes fueron encontrados por Sternberg en 1928, en la Formación Dinosaur Park de Alberta.

facts.statement: Dale Russell described a more complete skeleton in 1969 from the Dinosaur Park Formation, which formed the scientific basis for a famous life-sized sculpture accompanied by the fictional humanoid descendant "Dinosauria".
facts.quote: Dale Russell describió un esqueleto más completo de Stenonychosaurus en 1969 a partir de la Formación Dinosaur Park , que finalmente formó la base científica para una famosa escultura de tamaño natural de Stenonychosaurus acompañada por su descendiente humanoide ficticio, el "Dinosauroide".

facts.statement: Sternberg initially classified Stenonychosaurus as a member of the family Coeluridae.
facts.quote: Sternberg inicialmente clasificó a Stenonychosaurus como miembro de la familia Coeluridae.

facts.statement: Together with Saurornithoides, it formed the family Saurornithoididae.
facts.quote: Junto con Saurornithoides, formó la familia Saurornithoididae.

facts.statement: In 2017, Van der Reest and Currie found that Stenonychosaurus was a valid genus but reassigned much of the known material to the new genus Latenivenatrix.
facts.quote: En 2017, Van der Reest y Currie encontraron que Stenonychosaurus era un género válido, pero reasignaron gran parte del material conocido al nuevo género Latenivenatrix.

facts.statement: A 2021 analysis determined that characters previously diagnostic of Latenivenatrix were actually individual variables, the two taxa overlap stratigraphically, and Latenivenatrix mcmasterae is a junior synonym of Stenonychosaurus inequalis.
facts.quote: En 2021, un nuevo análisis más completo de la morfología y las posiciones estratigráficas del material esquelético conocido asignado a Stenonychosaurus y Latenivenatrix determinó que varios caracteres descritos como diagnósticos de Latenivenatrix son de hecho variables individuales, que ambos taxones se superponen estratigráficamente y que Latenivenatrix mcmasterae es un sinónimo menor de Stenonychosaurus inequalis.

facts.statement: A notable feature of these remains was the enlarged claw on the second toe, now recognized as a characteristic of early paravians.
facts.quote: Una característica notable de estos restos fue la garra agrandada en el segundo dedo del pie, que ahora se reconoce como característica de los primeros paravianos.

facts.statement: In 2011, Zanno and colleagues noted that numerous specimens currently assigned to Troodon formosus likely represent many new species, though a more exhaustive review of the specimens is required.
facts.quote: En 2011, Zanno y sus colegas revisaron la enrevesada historia de la clasificación de troodóntidos en el Cretácico superior de América del Norte. Siguieron al trabajo de Longrich de 2008 al tratar a Pectinodon bakkeri como un género válido, y señalaron que es probable que los numerosos especímenes del Cretácico superior actualmente asignados a Troodon formosus representen casi con seguridad numerosas especies nuevas, pero que se requiere una revisión más exhaustiva de los especímenes.

facts.statement: Because the holotype of T. formosus is a single tooth, this may render Troodon a nomen dubium.
facts.quote: Debido a que el holotipo de T. formosus es un solo diente, esto puede convertir a Troodon en un nomen dubium.

facts.statement: It became a very well-known theropod in the 1980s when its feet and cranial box were described in more detail.
facts.quote: Stenonychosaurus se convirtió en un terópodo muy conocido en la década de 1980, cuando se describieron con más detalle los pies y la caja craneana.

facts.statement: In 1982, Dale A. Russell hypothesized an evolutionary path for Stenonychosaurus if it had not died out in the Cretaceous-Paleogene extinction event.
facts.quote: En 1982, Dale A. Russell, entonces curador de fósiles de vertebrados en el Museo Nacional de Canadá en Ottawa, conjeturó un posible camino evolutivo para Stenonychosaurus

facts.statement: Paleontologists have criticized Russell's hypothesis since the 1980s, arguing his proposed 'Dinosauroid' was too anthropomorphic.
facts.quote: Sin embargo, el experimento mental de Russell ha recibido críticas de otros paleontólogos desde la década de 1980, muchos de los cuales señalan que su "Dinosaurioide" es demasiado antropomórfico

facts.statement: In its original 1932 description, Stenonychosaurus was initially classified as a member of the family Coeluridae.
facts.quote: En la descripción original de 1932 inicialmente clasificó a Stenonychosaurus como miembro de la familia Coeluridae

facts.statement: It was not until 1969 that Russell classified Stenonychosaurus as a member of Troodontidae.
facts.quote: No fue hasta 1969 que Russell lo clasificó como miembro de Troodontidae

facts.statement: In 2017, Evans and colleagues suggested that Stenonychosaurus refers to troodontid skeletal material from the Dinosaur Park Formation.
facts.quote: En 2017, Evans y sus colegas sugirieron que Stenonychosaurus se usara para el material esquelético de troodontidos de la Formación Dinosaur Park

facts.statement: In the same year, van der Reest and Currie placed Stenonychosaurus in Troodontinae as a sister taxon to the clade formed by Saurornithoides and Zanabazar.
facts.quote: Ese mismo añovan der Reest y Currie colocaron a Stenonychosaurus en Troodontinae

facts.statement: The parent group of the genus Stenonychosaurus is Troodontini.
facts.quote: Parent group: Troodontini

facts.statement: Stenonychosaurus belongs to the family Troodontidae.
facts.quote: Family: Troodontidae

facts.statement: Stenonychosaurus lived during the Campanian to Maastrichtian stages, from 83.6 to 66 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Campanian to Maastrichtian (83.6 to 66 million years ago)

facts.statement: Stenonychosaurus inequalis is known from the Dinosaur Park Formation in southern Alberta, Canada.
facts.quote: Stenonychosaurus inequalis se conoce de la Formación Dinosaur Park del sur de Alberta, Canadá

facts.statement: At that time, the habitat was a warm coastal alluvial plain covered by temperate forests.
facts.quote: que en ese momento era una cálida llanura aluvial costera cubierta por bosques templados

facts.statement: Stenonychosaurus is believed to have been a predator, supported by its sickle-shaped toe claw.
facts.quote: Se cree que los Stenonychosaurus eran depredadores , una opinión respaldada por su garra en forma de hoz en el pie

facts.statement: A comparative study of the feeding apparatus suggests Stenonychosaurus may have been an omnivore.
facts.quote: Un estudio comparativo del aparato de alimentación sugiere que Stenonychosaurus podría haber sido un omnívoro

facts.statement: The jaws joined in a wide U-shaped symphysis similar to that of an iguana, a lizard adapted to a herbivorous lifestyle.
facts.quote: Las mandíbulas se unían en una amplia sínfisis en forma de U similar a la de una iguana, una especie de lagarto adaptada a un estilo de vida herbívoro

facts.statement: The teeth of Stenonychosaurus had large ridges, each called a denticule.
facts.quote: Los dientes de Stenonychosaurus tenían grandes estrías, cada una de las cuales se llama dentículo

facts.statement: A partial skeleton with preserved bite marks, possibly inflicted by a predator, has been discovered.
facts.quote: Se ha descubierto un esqueleto parcial con marcas de mordidas conservadas, posiblemente infligidas por un depredador

facts.statement: Age determination studies using growth ring counts suggest this dinosaur reached adult size in 3 to 5 years.
facts.quote: Los estudios de determinación de la edad realizados en el troodóntido de Dos medicinas utilizando recuentos de anillos de crecimiento sugieren que este dinosaurio alcanzó su tamaño adulto probablemente en 3 a 5 años
